name: nuxt-layer-annotation-inbox
description: Dev-only annotation toolbar whose notes land in .data/annotations/ with SFC source locations, for coding agents
//exports: Three entries, and each one is a different answer to `who compiles this file`. `.` is the layer itself, handed to Nuxt, which reads `nuxt.config.ts` as TypeScript. `./vite` is built to `dist/`, because it is the only entry a plain `vite.config.ts` loads through Node, and Node refuses to type-strip TypeScript under `node_modules`. `./mount` is raw source on purpose: the consumer's Vite is its compiler, and pre-bundling it would risk the `import.meta.env.DEV` dead-branch elimination that is what keeps the toolbar out of production builds. `main` stays beside the map for tools that predate exports.
//scripts: `prepare` rather than `prepack`, because npm runs `prepare` in two places this package depends on: for a workspace member on a root install, and for a git dependency after it is cloned. A package installed straight from GitHub therefore arrives with `dist/` built, which is how the consuming repo takes it once this layer is extracted.
//peerDependencies: Everything the layer imports from its host and must not bring a second copy of: `@nuxt/kit` in `modules/annotation-inbox/index.ts`, `searchForWorkspaceRoot` from `vite` in `vite.ts`, and `vue` dynamically in `runtime/mount.ts`. None of them were declared before, which worked only because every host this layer had ever been dropped into happened to have all four.
